chapter: Big Eye Nelson, Lutton's and Adams
title: The Bocage family band and Peter Bocage's manner
summary: He discusses who played in the Bocage band, Eddie Pearson and Pete's harsh teaching, and prefers his own style.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You were still playing with Bocas at the time? You were playing with Peter Bocas too? No, not at that time. Who was playing with Peter Bocas?

Well that was mostly a family band. It was either Lou Warner and what was the bull card saxophone player, but Charlie, Henry, Pete, those three were standards. Alfred Whitting was the standard drummer most of the time.
Eddie Pearson was a nephew. Yeah, he was a nephew. And Minetta told me that Pete told Eddie he was a bonehead and he never would learn how to play drum.
So he went to Minetta. That's right, he went to Minetta. I don't think I'd like it if my uncle told me I was a bonehead.
No, I wouldn't like it, Peter. He was really mean to people like that.
Well he was all right if you understood him.
You understand? Well I understood him. I used to get mad and do things. Once you understand a guy, well you know how to teach. Well he was a good friend of mine. That's all.
Yeah, but outside of that he was all right.
I was kind of fine with him. The only thing, just like I said, I wasn't used to that well playing. Right now if you're playing with another guy you got to do what he said he was doing.
Which way do you prefer to play yourself? My original style. Yeah, because I'm used to it.
